sources.title: Gabriel Peyré and Marco Cuturi, Computational Optimal Transport

author_read_locators.locator: §2.1 probability simplex and discrete measures; §2.3 equations (2.10)–(2.11) and marginal notation; complete relevant §3.1 equations (3.2)–(3.3) and Remark 3.2.
author_read_locators.disposition: Used the finite histogram convention, coupling matrix, marginal constraints, primal cost and dual linear program as source context. Remark 3.2 explicitly sends strong duality to an external LP theorem; that theorem is not imported. The authored cone-separation proof supplies the complete finite result.

author_read_locators.locator: §3.3 Proposition 3.2 and its complete proof, equations for the zero primal-dual gap; §6.1 Proposition 6.1 and its complete proof, equations (6.1)–(6.2).
author_read_locators.disposition: Used the source's complementary-slackness characterization and discrete one-potential/Lipschitz formulation as independent checks of the local claims. The source proof of complementary slackness assumes strong duality; the local theorem first proves that equality itself.

sources.title: Filippo Santambrogio, Introduction to Optimal Transport Theory

author_read_locators.locator: Complete relevant §§1.1–1.2, PDF pp. 3–5: Kantorovich plans, primal cost, two-potential dual, formal inf-sup exchange and Proposition 1.1.
author_read_locators.disposition: The notes give the transport-plan interface and dual form. They explicitly state that the inf-sup exchange hypotheses are not checked and that the notes treat Euclidean domains rather than arbitrary metric spaces. Those omissions are not imported: the finite arbitrary-metric result is proved locally.

author_read_locators.locator: Complete §1.3, PDF pp. 5–6: Proposition 1.2, proof that the p=1 c-transform equals the negative potential, and the one-Lipschitz dual expression.
author_read_locators.disposition: Used as a second independent treatment of the one-potential reduction. The local finite proof verifies the c-transform inequalities directly from the metric triangle inequality; no Euclidean embedding is assumed.

sources.title: Martin Arjovsky, Soumith Chintala and Léon Bottou, Wasserstein GAN, arXiv:1701.07875v3

author_read_locators.locator: §2, PDF pp. 3–5, Earth Mover distance and compact-metric KR dual formula; §3 and Theorem 3, PDF pp. 5–7.
author_read_locators.disposition: Used only to verify the compact-space machine-learning context and exact ideal-critic boundary. The paper invokes the known KR duality and does not prove the finite theorem; WGAN differentiability, training, and neural-critic conclusions are out of scope.

author_read_locators.locator: Appendix C, complete proof of Theorem 3, PDF pp. 23–24.
author_read_locators.disposition: Read only to verify the excluded WGAN claim boundary. The proof assumes compact data space, invokes the compact-metric KR dual, applies an envelope theorem, and uses Assumption 1 for almost-everywhere differentiability and dominated differentiation; none of these WGAN conclusions is imported into the finite-metric item.

sources.title: Wouter Kager, A Short Simple Proof of Closedness of Convex Cones and Farkas' Lemma, arXiv:2208.11678v2

author_read_locators.locator: Complete two-page publication, PDF pp. 1–2, finite generated-cone closedness lemma and proof.
author_read_locators.disposition: Confirms the finite-cone closedness statement. Kager's proof uses a normalized minimizing-support sequence and Bolzano–Weierstrass; the authored lemma instead gives a finite support-elimination and Gram-matrix proof, preserving the choice-free argument.
